questions.question: A user copies styled text from a web page but wants plain, unformatted text pasted into their document — not the source's fonts and colors. Which shortcut pastes without formatting?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+Shift+V pastes clipboard content as plain text in browsers and many editors.

questions.question: A Windows user copied three items earlier and wants to paste the second one — not just the most recent. Which shortcut opens the clipboard history panel?
questions.explanation: Win+V opens the Windows clipboard history, listing recently copied items.

questions.question: A user wants a bird's-eye view of every open window plus both virtual desktops so they can drag a window between them. Which shortcut opens Task View?
questions.explanation: Win+Tab opens Task View, showing all windows and virtual desktops.

questions.question: Before a demo, a presenter wants a fresh, empty desktop for slides while their email stays open on the first one. Which shortcut creates a new virtual desktop?
questions.explanation: Win+Ctrl+D spawns a new virtual desktop and switches to it.

questions.question: A technician must launch devmgmt.msc quickly without browsing menus. Which shortcut opens the Run dialog to type it in?
questions.explanation: Win+R opens the Run box for launching programs by name.

questions.question: A support script instructs 'open Settings, then Bluetooth.' Which single shortcut opens the Windows Settings app directly?
questions.explanation: Win+I launches the Settings app in Windows 10 and 11.

questions.question: A user must find a site they visited last week by scanning every page visited. Which browser shortcut opens the history page?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+H opens the browsing history page in most browsers.

questions.question: A user downloaded an installer an hour ago and wants the browser's download list to re-run it. Which shortcut opens the downloads page?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+J opens the downloads page in Chrome and Edge.

questions.question: Before returning a shared PC, a user must wipe cookies and cached pages via the browser's cleanup dialog. Which shortcut opens it directly?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+Shift+Delete opens the 'clear browsing data' dialog in most browsers.

questions.question: A web developer must inspect a misbehaving page's console and DOM without navigating menus. Which single key launches the developer tools?
questions.explanation: F12 toggles developer tools in most browsers.

questions.question: A user cycling through browser tabs overshoots by one; instead of looping forward through 20 tabs, which shortcut steps one tab back?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+Shift+Tab moves to the previous tab while Ctrl+Tab moves forward.

questions.question: A user's rightmost browser tab is pinned documentation they need instantly, no matter how many tabs are open. Which shortcut jumps straight to the last tab?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+9 selects the last tab; Ctrl+1 through Ctrl+8 select tabs by position.

questions.question: A researcher drilled five links deep and wants to return one page without retyping the URL or reaching for the mouse. Which shortcut navigates Back?
questions.explanation: Alt+Left Arrow triggers the browser's Back action.

questions.question: To compare two documents side-by-side, a user wants the current window pinned to the left half of the screen. Which shortcut snaps it there?
questions.explanation: Win+Left snaps the active window to the left half of the screen.

questions.question: A kiosk keyboard's Windows key is disabled, but the technician still needs the Start menu. Which alternate key combination opens it?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+Esc opens the Start menu — the fallback for a missing or disabled Win key.

questions.question: During a presentation, a Windows user must switch the projector to 'Duplicate' or 'Second screen only' instantly. Which shortcut opens the projection menu?
questions.explanation: Win+P opens the Project flyout offering PC screen only, Duplicate, Extend, and Second screen only.

questions.question: A user wants to screenshot only the currently active window to the clipboard rather than the whole screen. Which shortcut does this?
questions.explanation: Alt+Print Screen captures only the focused window; Print Screen alone grabs the entire display.

questions.question: A presenter needs the entire Windows screen — not just browser content — to zoom in. Which shortcut activates Magnifier zoom-in?
questions.explanation: Win+Plus launches the Magnifier and zooms the whole desktop; Win+Esc closes it.

questions.question: The third app pinned to a Windows taskbar must open instantly without the mouse. Which shortcut launches it?
questions.explanation: Win+number launches or switches to the app pinned at that taskbar position; Win+3 opens the third.

questions.question: A cluttered desktop must be cleared while keeping only the active window visible. Which Windows shortcut minimizes every other window?
questions.explanation: Win+Home minimizes all windows except the active one; pressing it again restores them.
